en: [GAUTAMA DHARMA SŪTRA 1.1] GAUTAMA DHARMA SŪTRA 1.1.1: The Veda is the root of Dharma. GAUTAMA DHARMA SŪTRA 1.1.2: And the tradition and conduct of those who know it.
Gautama 1.3: A transgression of dharma and great acts of violence are observed even among the great; [this is so] because there is no visible purpose [in them].
Gautama 1.4: This is due to the weakness of those who follow later.
Gautama Sūtra 1.4: When there is a conflict between rules of equal authority, there is an option.
Gautama Sūtra 1.5: The initiation ceremony (*upanayana*) for a Brāhmaṇa takes place in the eighth year.
Gautama Sūtra 1.6: In the ninth or the fifth year, it may be performed for the sake of a specific desire (*kāmya*).
Gautama 1.1.8: The number [of years] begins from conception.
Gautama 1.1.9: That is his second birth. Gautama 1.1.10: Because of that, he is called an *ācārya*.
And because of the recitation of the Vedas (Gautama Sūtra 1.10).
For the Kṣatriya and the Vaiśya, [the initiation] is at the eleventh or twelfth year (Gautama Sūtra 1.11).
The Sāvitrī is not lost for a Brāhmaṇa until the sixteenth year (Gautama Sūtra 1.12).
For a Kṣatriya, there are twenty-two [verses]; for a Vaiśya, two more than that. The girdles are made of muñja grass, a bowstring, and wool, respectively.
Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.16: The skins of the black antelope, the ruru deer, and the goat [are prescribed].
Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.17: The garments of all [students] may be made of hemp, linen, bark, or kutapa wool.
Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.18: And cotton [is also permitted], provided it is not processed (i.e., unwashed).
Gautama 1.1.19: Some say that even the saffron-colored garment [is permitted]. Gautama 1.1.20a: A tree-bark garment is for the Brāhmaṇa.
Gautama 1.1.20b: Madder-red and yellow garments are for the other two [castes].

Gautama 1.21–24: The staffs for a Brāhmaṇa are made of Bilva or Palāśa wood; for the remaining [castes], they are made of Aśvattha or Pīlu wood; or, alternatively, a staff suitable for sacrifice may be used by all.
Gautama Sūtra 1.25: [The sacrificial posts] should be unblemished, curved like a sacrificial post, and provided with bark.
Gautama Sūtra 1.26: They should be measured by the height of the head, the forehead, or the tip of the nose.
Gautama Sūtra 1.27: And [the ascetics] may have shaven heads, matted hair, or a single tuft of matted hair on the crown.
Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.27–30: One who has something in hand while being impure from food remnants (ucchiṣṭa) shall perform ācamana without setting it down.
Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.29: The purification of objects made of metal, clay, wood, and woven cloth is by means of scrubbing, heating, scraping, and washing, respectively.
Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.30: Stones, gems, shells, and pearls are purified in the same manner as articles made of metal.

Gautama 1.1.32: [The purification] of cloth, ropes, split bamboo, and leather is like that of cloth.
Gautama 1.1.33: Or there is the discarding of those items that are excessively defiled.
Gautama 1.1.34: One should begin the act of purification facing either the east or the north.

Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.35–36: Seated in a clean place, having placed his right arm between his knees and wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder, he should wash both hands up to the wrists; then, restraining his speech and touching his heart, he should sip water three or four times.
He should wipe his mouth twice.
He should wipe his feet and sprinkle them with water;
he should also touch the cavities of the head.
And he should place [the water] on his head (GautDhS 1.36).
After sleeping, eating, or sneezing, he should do so again (GautDhS 1.37).
Regarding food particles stuck between the teeth, it is as if they were still in the mouth, except when they have been touched by the tongue (GautDhS 1.38).
Gautama 1.1.42: Some say [the mouth remains impure] until the spittle falls.
Gautama 1.1.43: One should know that in the case of fallen drops, as in the case of [fluids like] *āsrāva*, one becomes pure even while swallowing them.
Gautama 1.1.46: Primary droplets do not cause one to become ritually impure (*ucchiṣṭa*), provided they do not fall upon a limb of the body.
Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.42: Purity regarding an impure substance consists in the removal of its stains and odor.
Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.43: That [removal] is first performed with water and with earth.
Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.44: And [this applies] in cases of contact with urine, feces, oily secretions, discharges, and food.
And where the sacred tradition (āmnāya) may prescribe [a rule], [one should act accordingly].
Having grasped the left hand of the teacher with his own hand, excluding the thumb, he should address the teacher, saying: "Recite, sir! (adhīhi bhoḥ).

Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.48: [There shall be] touching of the vital breaths with *darbha* grass.
Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.49: Three breath-restraints (*prāṇāyāma*), each consisting of fifteen measures (*mātrā*).
Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.50: And the sitting posture upon [grass] whose tips point toward the east.
Gautama Sūtra 1.51: *Oṃ*. The five preceding *vyāhṛtis* end with *satya*.
Gautama Sūtra 1.52: In the morning, there is the clasping of the teacher’s feet.
Gautama 1.1.54: And at the beginning and the end of the recitation of the *brahman*, [the teacher should say "Recite"].
Gautama 1.1.55: Having been permitted, the disciple should sit to the south, facing east, or facing north.
Gautama 1.1.56: And the recitation of the *Sāvitrī* [is performed].
Gautama Sūtra 1.56: At the beginning, when taking up the Veda, [the syllable *oṃ* is used].
Gautama Sūtra 1.57: The syllable *oṃ* is used even elsewhere.
Gautama Sūtra 1.58: If he goes between [the teacher and the fire], there must be a renewed formal sitting (initiation).

Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.1.60–61: In the case of the death of a dog, a mongoose, a snake, a frog, or a cat occurring within the period of impurity, there shall be a three-day fast and a temporary departure from the village.
For other animals, the penance consists of breath-control exercises (*prāṇāyāma*) and the consumption of clarified butter (*ghṛtaprāśana*).
And likewise when studying near a cremation ground.
[GautAA 1,2 = GautSt II]
Gautama 1.2.1: Before initiation, there is freedom of action, freedom of speech, and freedom of consumption.
Gautama 1.2.2: [This applies] except for what is unfit for sacrifice.
Gautama Sūtra 1.2.3: He is a student of sacred knowledge (*brahmacārī*).
Gautama Sūtra 1.2.4: His discharge of urine and feces is performed as prescribed.
Gautama Sūtra 1.2.5: For him, the rule for ritual sipping (ācamana) does not exist.
Gautama Sūtra 1.2.6: Except for wiping, washing, and sprinkling.
Gautama Sūtra 1.2.7: There is no impurity resulting from touching him.

Gautama 1.2.8: But one should not employ him for the offering into the sacred fire (*agnihotra*) or for the presentation of the sacrificial oblation (*bali*). Gautama 1.2.9: One should not cause him to recite the *brahman* formula, except at the pouring of the *svadhā* libation.
Gautama 1.2.10: The rule [of silence] begins from the initiation (*upanayana*).
Gautama Dharmasūtra 1.2.11: Celibacy has been described.
Gautama Dharmasūtra 1.2.12: Tending the sacred fire, kindling the fire, and going for alms.
Gautama Dharmasūtra 1.2.13: Speaking the truth.
Gautama 1.2.14: Touching water. Gautama 1.2.15: Some [prescribe] the Godāna ceremony and so forth. Gautama 1.2.16: And being outside during the twilight prayers (*saṃdhyā*).
Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.2.17: He should stand during the first part of the night and sit during the latter part, remaining silent until the stars appear or the dawn light is seen.
Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.2.18: He should not look at the sun.

Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.2.19: He should avoid honey, meat, perfumes, garlands, sleeping by day, anointing the body, riding in vehicles, wearing shoes, using an umbrella, lust, anger, greed, delusion, idle talk, playing musical instruments, bathing for pleasure, cleaning the teeth, exhilaration, dancing, singing, slander, and fear.
Gautama 1.2.20 / Gautama Dharma Sūtra 2.14: Covering one's neck, using a cloth sling across the knees, leaning against something, and stretching out the feet in the presence of the teacher;
Gautama 1.2.21 / Gautama Dharma Sūtra 2.15: Spitting, laughing, yawning, and cracking the knuckles.
Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.2.22 / 2.16: Looking at or touching a woman when there is a suspicion of sexual intercourse.
Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.2.23 / 2.17: Gambling, associating with the low-born, taking what is not given, and violence.
Gautama 1.2.24: [One should avoid using] the names of one's teacher, his son, women, and those initiated for sacrifice.
Gautama 1.2.25a: [One should avoid] harsh speech. (Variant:
"corrupt speech")
A Brāhmaṇa must always abstain from intoxicating liquor. He should sleep on a low bed or seat, rise before [his teacher], and go to rest after him. He should be restrained in speech, arms, and belly.
Gautama 1.2.28: One should mention the name and the lineage of one's teacher with respect. Gautama 1.2.29: The same applies when honoring [the teacher] or when [he is] superior.
Gautama 1.2.30: One should respond [to a command] after rising from one's bed, seat, or standing place.
Gautama Sūtra 1.2.31 / Gautama Dharma Sūtra 2.26: Approaching [the teacher] is prescribed because of a specific injunction; it is performed for an invisible (transcendental) purpose.

Gautama Sūtra 1.2.32 / Gautama Dharma Sūtra 2.27: He should remain standing with his body lowered, or sitting, when he is in the presence of the teacher; he should rise upon seeing the teacher, even while engaged in inhaling or exhaling air horizontally (i.e., sitting).

Gautama 1.2.33: He should follow one who is departing. Gautama 1.2.34: Having informed [the teacher] of his task and announced it. Gautama 1.2.35: When summoned, he should study. Gautama Sūtra 2.28a: [He should follow one who is departing. Gautama Sūtra 2.28b: Having informed [the teacher] of his task and announced it. Gautama Sūtra 2.29: When summoned, he should study.
One who studies when summoned;
being intent upon what is pleasing and beneficial;
and likewise toward his wife and sons.
Gautama 1.2.38: [The pupil shall not perform] eating the leftovers [of the teacher], bathing [him], adorning him, washing his feet, massaging him, or clasping his feet.
Gautama 1.2.39: Upon returning from a journey abroad, he should clasp the feet of the wives of his teachers.
Gautama 1.2.40: According to some, this does not apply to young wives, provided he has attained the age of discretion.
Gautama Dharmasūtra 1.2.41 / 2.35: He should wander for alms among all castes, excluding those who are accused of crimes or those who have fallen from their caste.
Gautama Dharmasūtra 1.2.42 / 2.36: The word *bhavat* (sir) should be employed at the beginning, middle, and end [of the request], according to the order of the castes.
Gautama-Dharmasūtra 1.2.43 / Gautama-Stotra 2.37: In the absence [of a teacher], [one may seek instruction] with others among teachers, paternal kinsmen, or gurus.
Gautama-Dharmasūtra 1.2.44 / Gautama-Stotra 2.38: Among these, one should avoid each preceding one [in preference for the following].
Gautama Dharmasūtra 1.2.45: Having offered [the food] to his teacher and being permitted by him, he should eat.
Gautama Dharmasūtra 1.2.46: In the teacher's absence, [he should offer it] to his wife, his son, or a fellow student.

Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.2.47: Restraining his speech, being satisfied with what he receives and not coveting more, he should keep water close at hand. Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.2.48: The instruction of a pupil is carried out without corporal punishment. Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.2.49: In case of incapacity [to control him], [the teacher may use] a thin rope or a split bamboo cane.
Gautama Dharma Sūtra 1.2.50 / Gautama Dharma Sūtra 2.44: One who strikes with anything other than a rope, a bamboo cane,
or a leaf is to be punished by the king.

Gautama 1.2.51: He shall observe the life of a religious student (*brahmacarya*) for twelve years with respect to one Veda. Gautama 1.2.52: Or he may do so for twelve years for each of all the Vedas. Gautama 1.2.53: Or until he has mastered them.

Gautama 1.2.54 / Gautama Dharmasūtra 2.48: At the conclusion of his studies, the teacher should be invited with a gift. Gautama 1.2.55 / Gautama Dharmasūtra 2.49: Or, having performed [the ritual], the student may bathe with the teacher’s permission. Gautama 3.10.37: Even the son of a Śūdra woman, if he is obedient, shall receive a means of subsistence from one who has no other offspring, according to the rule for a pupil (antevāsin). Gautama 3.10.38: According to some, even the son of a wife of equal caste (savarṇā) does not receive it if he conducts himself improperly.
Gautama 3.10.39: The Vedic scholars (*śrotriya*) shall divide the inheritance of a childless Brāhmaṇa. Gautama 3.10.40: For others [than Brāhmaṇas], the king [shall take it].
Gautama 3.10.41: Those who are mentally deficient (*jaḍa*) or impotent (*klība*) shall be maintained.
The offspring of one who is mentally deficient is entitled to a share.

The same applies to those born of women in the inverse order of castes (*pratiloma*), as in the case of the son of a *śūdra* woman. There is no division of water, of what is acquired for common welfare, and of prepared food.
And [the same applies] when women are engaged [in the act].
When [a rite] is unknown, it should be performed as recommended by at least ten learned men who are experts in *ūha* (adaptation), free from greed, and of good character.

Gautama 3.10.47 / Gautama 28.49: Four who have mastered the four Vedas, three of whom are householders from among the [four] stages of life, and three who are individually learned in the Dharma—these ten at minimum, they call an assembly (*pariṣad*).
(Note: *VAR_St*: "three" refers to these).
Gautama 3.10.48: But in the absence of these [elders], a *śrotriya* who is learned in the Veda and distinguished in case of conflicting opinions—what he says [is authoritative].
Gautama 3.10.49: For from him [proceeds] this power over living beings in matters of harming or favoring them.
Gautama 3.10.50: Through knowledge and devotion, one who knows the Dharma especially attains the heavenly world among those who possess dharma.
"Thus, this is Dharma, this is Dharma. Gautama 3.10.51.
